title: Migrate the batch runner's ABORT/CONTINUE/RETRY error semantics
target_requirement: Reimplement the legacy sequential batch runner as a Python module exposing run_jobs(jobs, executor) -> log, where the injected executor raises on failure: jobs run strictly in list order; ABORT stops the whole schedule; CONTINUE logs BATCH_ROWSKIP and proceeds; RETRY:n re-invokes up to n additional times (n+1 total) and aborts the schedule if still failing; the log records exact attempt counts and outcomes per attempted job.
expected_behavior: run_jobs returns one {name, attempts, outcome ok|skip|abort, audits} entry per attempted job in order; after an abort no later job is executed or logged; a CONTINUE failure carries audits ['BATCH_ROWSKIP'] and the next job still runs; a RETRY:2 job failing twice then succeeding logs attempts 3 outcome ok; attempts always equals the executor invocation count; job exceptions never propagate out of the runner.
provenance: Synthetic; authored for LegacyCRM-Bench from Meridian CRM 4.2 spec (SYSTEM_OVERVIEW.md §7) and batch_jobs.cfg.
security_expectations: No network access; the runner must not import network or subprocess modules and must not sleep (retries are immediate and deterministic).
failure_conditions: Executing jobs after an abort; retrying more or fewer than n additional times; logging BATCH_ROWSKIP for successful or aborted jobs; letting executor exceptions propagate; reordering jobs; wall-clock dependence.
